text.p: Following are some of the main
stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified
these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Planned merger between sanitaryware producer Sphinx
Gustavsberg and Switzerland's Keramik Laufen abandoned. (p1)
- U.S. truck maker Paccar makes friendly 933 mln guilder
takeover bid for DAF Trucks. (p1)
- South Korean industrial conglomerate Samsung wants to wrap
up planned takeover of Dutch planemaker Fokker quickly. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell's U.S. unit Shell Oil in talks with
rivals Texaco and Star Enterprise on merging their U.S. refining
and marketing activities. (p1)
- Shipbuilders Van der Giessen-de Noord and Wilton Fijenoord
break off merger talks. (p1)
- Recovery of KLM's cargo traffic continues with seven
percent growth in September. (p3)
- Industrial group SHV's unit SHV Energy seeks to boost its
51.6 pct stake in U.K. energy company Calor to 100 pct. (p4)
- Electronic financial information publisher Bloomberg is
not interested in a merger with publisher Reed Elsevier. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Belgium's foreign affairs minister wonders whether there
will be enough time during Dutch presidency of EU in first half
of 1997 to revise the Maastricht treaty. (p1)
- Two largest Internet providers in the Netherlands Planet
Internet and World Access to merge. (p2)
- Chemicals concern Akzo Nobel denies having stolen solar
cell technology from small company Chip Market. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Transport minister gives cable company Edon/CasTel of
Groningen licence to set up a regional telecom network. (p25)
- Unilever opens research laboratory in Shanghai, China.
- Special team at KLM explores scope for further cost
savings. (p27)
- Heavy trade in bio-tech company Artu Biological shares.
TROUW
- Government starts campaign to inform businesses about
imminent launch of the single European currency, the Euro. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Rival banks furious at ABN Amro for its privileged access
to detailed financial information ahead of entertainment company
Endemol's bourse flotation. (p12)
- KLM optimistic about patching up disturbed relationship
with its U.S. partner Northwest Airlines. (13)
